counterfactual_missing_items: No acute abnormality of the pancreas
Serum ketones/arterial blood gas or anion-gap measurement
Endoscopic confirmation of a peptic ulcer
decisive_items: progressively worsening sharp epigastric pain radiating to the back
response.rationale: R5 combines the two most specific raw findings: classic epigastric pain radiating to the back and markedly elevated lipase, which jointly satisfy acute pancreatitis despite a normal or unrevealing CT; early/mild pancreatitis can be CT-negative. R6 only captures epigastric pain and pantoprazole non-response, but does not explain the acute lipase elevation or overall syndrome. The other candidates rest on known CKD, diabetes history, or nonspecific chronic features rather than the acute presentation.

rejected.why: This is only an append-only completion of known CKD stage 4; it does not address the acute epigastric pain or elevated lipase.
DKA would require ketosis or metabolic acidosis, which are not shown, and the diabetes/hyperglycemia is nonspecific in this context.
Pancreatic insufficiency does not cause acute epigastric pain and prominent lipase elevation without malabsorptive chronic features.
Known CKD and elevated creatinine reflect baseline renal disease and do not explain the acute pancreatic/toxic clinical syndrome.
